s0157: The concept behind the Sapporo International AI Film Festival, how the festival is structured (Bathe in Stories / Know Your Creativity / Ignite the Future), Incubation, the organizers, and how to contact us.
s0160: A compass, and a festival flame, for an age in which the power to create is open to everyone.
s0165: The Sapporo International AI Film Festival is a flame.
s0166:
A festival flame for experiencing and honoring the stories born from people who have taken up new ways to create,
and for kindling, from those stories, the next creators and the next stories to come.
s0167: Since the dawn of time, humans have carried stories in their heads.
s0168:
A landscape never seen.
A person who does not yet exist.
A memory that won't fade.
A feeling that words can't hold.
A world you want to show someone.
s0169: Imagining has always been something anyone could do. Giving it form was another matter. Cameras, actors, crews, music, editing, CG, time, money. However vivid the world in your head, only a few could finish it as a film and deliver it to someone else.
s0170: Now, AI has broken that wall down. One person creates images from their own imagination. Creates sound. Creates voices. Brings characters to life. And raises a single story into being.
s0171: An age is beginning in which more people than ever can give their stories form.
s0172: What excites us is not AI itself. It's that people who always wanted to create but never had the means have become people who can. A student. An office worker. A musician, a painter, an engineer. Someone who has never made a film in their life can now turn the story inside them into moving images.
s0173: Not because AI creates in place of humans. Because the range over which the creativity sleeping inside a person can be carried out into the world has widened like never before.
s0174: The more widely the power to create is opened, the more one question matters.
s0175: What do you want to create?
s0176: You can make beautiful images. You can paint a vast world. You can finish a film alone. That is a real and enormous change. But that alone doesn't move people. Why tell this story? What feeling do you want to leave with the viewer? The more technology we can use, the more human the question that remains at the end.
s0177: So what we are truly looking for is not the category of "AI film" itself. It might be a film. It might be animation. It might be music, a game, an interactive experience. The form of expression can change. The technology can change.
s0178: At the center of it all stands a human being trying to tell someone something.
s0179: Film is not something you merely "watch." In the dark, a world rises on the big screen. Sound resonates through your body. Someone beside you gasps, laughs, cries. Same time, same place, one story shared with a crowd. There are moments, possible only in a cinema, when you experience a story with your whole body.
s0180: Precisely because streaming lets us reach films anytime, anywhere, a festival still has meaning. When a film arrives at that moment, the technology recedes into the background. What remains is the work, the story, and whatever is born between the person who made it and the person who received it.
s0181: What we want to see is not a race of technical specs.
s0182:
What will people create, now that they hold a new power?
And how far can those stories move the human heart?
s0183:
What will you create?
Show us. We'll watch every single one.

s0186: Screenings, talks, and the reception are designed not as independent events but as a single flow.
s0188: The Final Selection films are screened on the big screen of the hitaru theater and are eligible for the awards. The Second Selection films are screened (free of charge) at SCARTS. Award-winning films are released online after the festival. We experience films gathered from all over the world together with the audience, taking in each work whole, with the laughter, the silence, the surprise, and the tension of the room. Not simply watching, but bathing in the story.
s0189: In the judging, what matters is not merely which AI or technology was used, but what the work depicts, what kind of experience it creates, and how far it moves the audience.
s0191: Film directors, animators, video artists, AI creators: people who actually use AI in film production share how they think, what they struggle with, and what they have tried.
s0192: This is not a lecture where you listen to a famous name and go home. By encountering the creativity of others, you come to know your own. Our aim is that between arriving and leaving, your list of "things I might be able to make, too" has grown a little.
s0194: Creators meet creators, of course, but also film meets music, creators meet companies, students meet professionals, Japan meets the world. People who usually work in separate places come together.
s0195: Not a mere social gathering, but the first step toward igniting the future. Film and robotics, video and tourism: from encounters that make you think "I never knew those could connect," things that did not yet exist that day begin to move.
s0197: The "& Incubation" in our name is not decoration. At this festival, we use "Incubation" to mean four things together: the talks (including live demonstrations), the Networking Reception, the online release of the award-winning films, and the cycle that leads to the next work.
s0198: Someone who came as an audience member is one day making films of their own. Two people who met at the reception are watching the film they made together on the screen. We hope to set that cycle in motion. Not just a place that gathers finished films and screens them, but a place where you experience stories, come to know your own creativity, and the next act of creation begins to move.
s0200: Encounter the ideas and the trial and error of creators, with live demonstrations. For first-timers, a moment of "maybe I can do this too" and a nudge toward that first film.
s0202: Creators, companies, students, and international guests meet, and the next film, team, job, or project begins.

s0245: What we want to see is a story.
s0246: Which AI you used, or how new the technology is, is not the subject of the judging. What does the work say, what experience does it create, and how far does it move the audience? We look at the power of the story first.
s0248: Why tell this story? What do you want to say? Has what lived inside the creator risen into being as a work?
s0250: The design of image, sound, and time. On the big screen, in the darkness of the theater, does the work become an experience the audience can bathe in?
s0251: How far did you move the heart?
s0252: Make them laugh. Make them cry. Surprise them. Make them think. Did you leave something with the viewer?
s0253: We look at technique insofar as it supports the story. How well the creator controlled the characteristic seams of AI, broken images or sound, inconsistencies in characters or worlds, and finished the work without compromising the experience. And the willingness to try new forms of expression. These are evaluated as secondary factors supporting the three points above.

s0511: Meet the people who have "finished a film with AI," all in one day
s0512: From entries submitted around the world, we invite the Final Selection creators to Sapporo. The people gathered here are those who have taken a film all the way to completion using AI. The Networking Reception, the booths in the theater foyer, the Sponsor Session. Whether you're hiring, commissioning, or co-creating, you'll meet people who speak your language, all on the same day.
s0513: Plant the "first flag" of AI film culture in Sapporo, with us
s0514: Filmmaking with generative AI is at the very moment of emerging as a culture. The Sapporo International AI Film Festival is its first edition. Only in the first few editions can you be on the side that, ten years from now, is said to be where Japan's AI film scene spread from. This is not an ad buy. It is an investment remembered as a founding act of culture. Your company's name remains in the closing credits after the screening.
s0515: Everyone you reach is a stakeholder
s0516: Some 1,000 people looking up at the big screen of Sapporo Cultural Arts Theater hitaru. People who watch the talk archive to the end. International entrants visiting our multilingual website. You reach only those who are making something with AI, want to, or want others to. This is reach in deep context, a different quality from the "caught my eye somehow" exposure of mass advertising.

s0739: Sapporo International AI Film Festival 2027 Production Guidelines: use of AI, legal compliance, copyright and rights, license for screening and streaming, privacy, prohibited content, transparency, and organizer decisions.
s0742: These guidelines apply to every film entered in the Sapporo International AI Film Festival 2027. They are the minimum rules for keeping AI filmmaking fun, honest, and comfortable for everyone involved. Please read them before you enter.
s0751: Back to the Call for Entries
s0752: The authoritative text of these Guidelines is the Japanese version. Versions in other languages, including this one, are reference translations; in the event of any discrepancy in interpretation, the Japanese text prevails.
s0753: All films entered in this festival must be suitable for all ages. We look forward to films that everyone, from children to adults, can enjoy with peace of mind.
s0756: FilmFreeway (public listing). No other entry channels are provided.
s0757: One film per person (or team). Up to two.
s0762: First-round review → Second Selection → Final Selection (theater screening, eligible for all awards). Announced April 15, 2027. The number of films selected is not disclosed.
s0764: This festival is for films made with generative AI as the primary production method. Films that use AI only for editing assistance or minor corrections may not fit the festival's purpose.
s0765: There is no limit on the type or number of AI tools you use. A single tool you picked up yesterday is fine. Please describe which AI you used and how in your film's information on FilmFreeway (description and question fields).
s0766: Combining AI-generated and live-action footage is permitted. Films that composite live action onto AI-generated imagery, or process live-action footage with AI, are welcome.
s0767: Any language may be used in your film. Beyond Japanese and English, we accept any form of linguistic expression, including fictional, constructed, or non-existent languages (films not in Japanese, or with unnatural Japanese, must include Japanese subtitles).
s0768: Films that use AI only for "invisible corrections" such as denoising or upscaling may not be recognized as AI films for the purposes of this festival.
s0769: Check the terms of service of the AI tools you use (commercial use, rights to generated output, etc.) yourself before entering. Take care with tools whose terms restrict use in films or public streaming.
s0771: Entrants must use generative AI in compliance with Japan's Copyright Act, the Act on the Protection of Personal Information, and other applicable laws. "Made with AI" is not a license for anything goes.
s0772: Please also keep in mind the spirit of the AI Guidelines for Business issued by Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications: human-centered, safe, transparent, and explainable. There's no need to overthink it, but make a habit of pausing whenever you wonder, "Is this okay?"
s0773: Reference links (all external sites, in Japanese)

s0775: Agency for Cultural Affairs: "Checklist & Guidance on AI and Copyright" (PDF)

s0777: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry: "Guidebook on the Use of Generative AI for Content Production" (PDF)
s0779: Entries must be original and must not use third-party copyrighted works, trademarks, characters, or similar without permission. Even with AI-generated material, uses that substantially imitate or reproduce existing works may constitute copyright infringement. Please respect the position set out by the Agency for Cultural Affairs and take care not to unfairly harm the interests of rights holders affected by AI training and generation.
s0780: Please confirm and complete the following rights clearances yourself before entering.
s0781: Copyright in video, still images, scripts, artwork, and so on
s0782: Copyright and master rights in any music and sound effects used (in addition to the venue screening, this festival plans to stream online via YouTube and similar platforms; make sure your license covers streaming, e.g. YouTube Audio Library, CC0, or properly licensed material)
s0783: Portrait and publicity rights where performers appear
s0784: Filming and usage permissions where real facilities, buildings, exhibits, and so on are filmed and used
s0785: Trademark and copyright considerations where corporate logos, brand names, product names, and so on are used
s0786: Prompts that imitate a specific artist, illustrator, or similar by name (we strongly recommend avoiding these from a rights-infringement standpoint)
s0787: Issues relating to the training data of the AI tools you use (subject to each tool provider's policies; the organizer accepts no responsibility for problems arising from them)
s0788: All rights clearance is the sole responsibility of the entrant. By entering, you warrant that your film does not infringe the rights of any third party and does not violate these guidelines. If a rights infringement or other issue comes to light after screening or streaming, the organizer may suspend publication of or remove the film in question.
s0789: 04Copyright Ownership and Use by the Organizer
s0790: Copyright in your film remains with you, the entrant. The organizer does not acquire any rights.
s0791: However, by entering, you are deemed to have granted the organizer permission to use and publish your film for the following purposes.
s0792: Screening on the venue screen (Sapporo Cultural Arts Theater hitaru) on the festival day (Final Selection films)
s0793: Screening at Sapporo Cultural Arts Community Center SCARTS (Court and Studio A / B) on the festival day (Second Selection films)
s0794: Online release of award-winning films after the festival (broadcast and archive publication on the official YouTube channel and other streaming platforms, including the early screening for crowdfunding supporters)
s0795: Use in festival publicity before and after the event (social media, the official website, promotional videos, press materials, etc.)
s0796: Adding the festival logo and credits to the film
s0797: Partial excerpts and edits for publicity and promotional purposes
s0798: Other uses reasonably deemed necessary for the operation of the festival
s0799: In these uses, the substance of the film will not be altered. The creator's name (a handle is fine) will be credited wherever possible.
s0800: 05Respect for Personal Information and Privacy
s0801: Using a real individual's facial photographs, voice, social media posts, or similar as AI training or generation material without their consent is prohibited. It may constitute a violation of privacy or portrait rights.
s0802: If you enter a film containing a "deepfake" that synthesizes the face or voice of a real person with AI, obtain that person's explicit consent and clearly state in the end credits or elsewhere that the film contains AI-synthesized depictions.
s0803: When depicting politicians, public figures, or deceased persons, expression that disregards their honor or dignity is not permitted.
s0804: Entrants who are minors must obtain the consent of a parent or guardian before entering.
s0806: All films entered in this festival must be suitable for all ages. Create your film on the assumption that a broad audience, including children, will watch it. Films containing any of the following may not be entered.
s0807: Content unsuitable for all-ages screening, such as sexual content, excessive violence, cruelty, or gore, or excessive horror
s0808: Content that violates the law, or that incites or encourages crime
s0809: Discrimination, hate speech, or incitement to violence
s0810: Expression intended to deliberately spread false information
s0811: Child pornography, revenge pornography, or other serious human rights violations
s0812: Expression that uncritically amplifies stereotypes relating to gender, race, origin, disability, and so on
s0813: Other content that offends public order and morals and is unfit for public screening
s0814: These prohibitions apply even to AI-generated material. The use of generative AI never justifies illegal or improper content.
s0816: List the AI tools you used in your film's information on FilmFreeway. Detailed descriptions of which tools you used and how will help in the judging (and we as organizers love learning about new ways of working).
s0817: If the organizer suspects a rights infringement or a violation of these guidelines, we may request additional explanation or supporting materials. Refusing to provide an explanation without good reason may result in exclusion from the selection.
s0819: If the organizer determines that a film seriously violates these guidelines, we may take measures such as exclusion from the selection, cancellation of the screening, or revocation of an award, even after the entry has been accepted. In such cases, we will notify the entrant of the reasons to the extent possible.
s0820: If the number of entries greatly exceeds expectations, the organizer may adjust the screening slots or screening method at its discretion.
s0821: Replacing a film after entry may be permitted at the organizer's discretion.
s0822: Final decisions on the interpretation and application of these guidelines rest with the organizer. If anything is unclear, feel free to ask us on Discord before you enter.
s0823: Screenings and streaming may be interrupted, or their content or schedule changed, due to technical problems, network conditions, venue facilities, or similar circumstances. Thank you for your understanding.
s0824: Questions? Ask us anytime on Discord
